goldens.comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
goldens.reasoning: C1 describes the same issue: negative slicing of a Django queryset in the optimized paginator.

goldens.comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
goldens.reasoning: C2 describes the same crash: accessing .has_global_access on a member that is None.

goldens.comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate covers math.floor/ceil being called on a datetime key.
No candidate covers the import of a class that doesn't exist.

candidates: When `enable_advanced_features=True` and `cursor.offset < 0`, line 882 executes `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and will raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported.` The comment on line 876 claiming the ORM handles this automatically is incorrect.

Accessing `organization_context.member.has_global_access` at line 71 throws `AttributeError` when `organization_context.member` is `None`, which happens when the user has no membership with the organization. The code should defensively check for `None` before accessing the attribute.
